text:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a lot of exporter cardinality from duplicated OTEL attributes added both at the edge gateway and again by workers. example: gateway adds `service.namespace`, worker adds `service.namespace` + `deployment.id`.

sam: Ugh. Do we have a pattern for canonicalizing attributes yet?

priya: Not formalized. Current quickfix was to drop gateway-added app-level attrs for async jobs, but that feels brittle.

maya: Agreed. Observed issues: exporters store both copies, sampling + retention dashboards get noisy. Also increases payload size for queued messages.

oliver: Could we centralize at the gateway and have workers only emit delta attributes? That requires a contract so workers can opt out of re-adding shared attrs.

sam: I prototyped a header-level flag `x-otel-canonical` that contains a short list of canonical keys the gateway owns. workers consult that and skip setting the keys if present. quick sketch: ```x-otel-canonical: service.namespace,env,team```

priya: That helps but two concerns: 1) queued retries may lose the header (SQS/SNS) 2) long-term we need a stable canonical list for compatibility with exporters.

maya: For 1) we should persist the canonical set in the message payload (small JSON field) in addition to headers for transports that strip headers. For 2) add a migration window where both are accepted.

srebot: Incident note — last month we had 30% spike in span payload size attributable to duplicate attrs on high-throughput ingestion. Putting idea to backlog.

oliver: Another option: normalize at the per-tenant exporter: exporter dedupes identical attr keys with same value from different start times. Pros: no changes to workers/gateway. Cons: exporter CPU and complexity + loss of origin info.

sam: I'd prefer gateway-led normalization because it avoids expanding telemetry payloads and is cheaper at scale. Implementation sketch: - gateway computes canonical set per-tenant - gateway attaches `x-otel-canonical` header + embed `__rt_canonical` JSON in message body for queues - update worker otel libs to respect header/body and skip writes for keys in the set - add a feature flag `telemetry.canonicalize.v1` behind a canary rollout

priya: Also consider the semantics: if worker needs to override a gateway value intentionally (e.g., enriched runtime metadata), allow `__rt_override` with `key:value` entries. Gateway should accept overrides by default but still include original in `meta.canonical_origin` for audit.

maya: Good point. We need auditability. Exporters should get `meta.canonical_origin` mapping: `{key: source}` so dashboards can filter by origin when diagnosing.

sam: I'll open a PR with the gateway changes: header + embedded JSON + feature flag. Canaries: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h; rollback on >1% drop in ingested spans or >2% increase in tail latency.

oliver: FYI I'll add a small exporter-side dedupe as a fallback for older tenants who don't opt in. Low CPU config by default.

priya: Tests to add: 1) header preserved across SQS/SNS republish 2) worker library respects header/body precedence 3) overrides honored and origin mapping present 4) end-to-end size regression test on synthetic workload

maya: Thanks — @sam link the PR and the runbook. After PR we should coordinate with metrics team to add a regression alert for span ingestion size and a query to compare attribute cardinality by tenant. :thumbsup:

sam: Will do. PR shortly.

otel-bot: Note: new spec draft saved to https://gist.github.com/redwood/otel-canonical-v1 — includes header names, message-body format, and migration timeline.
